cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Google Sign-In in an Android app is an OpenID Connect login across three parties: the app, Google and your backend. The app uses Credential Manager to get a Google ID token, a signed JWT proving who the user is.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: The app posts the ID token to the backend (for example /socialAuth/social-register). The backend verifies signature, expiry and audience with google-auth-library, then logs in an existing user or creates a new one (JIT provisioning). It then issues its own access and refresh tokens; the Google token is used only once.

questions.q: Why not use the Google ID token as the app's access token?
questions.a: Google issued it for sign-in with Google's rules. It expires in about an hour and you cannot revoke it when a user logs out or is banned.
Creating a new user record automatically the first time a verified Google user signs in.

questions.q: Which three checks does the backend make on the token?
questions.a: Valid signature, not expired, and issued for your client ID (audience).
